summary: Otto Blau worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg under August Friedrich Pott from circa 1848 to 1851.
Otto Fischer specialized in Sinology, Japanology, and history and archaeology. He held a post at the Kunstmuseum Basel in 1927 and taught at the University of Basel from circa 1927 to 1937.

Otto Franke was a scholar of Sinology and Indology. He studied at the University of Freiburg (~1883–1884) and the University of Göttingen (~1884–1888), later holding posts at the University of Hamburg (~1910–1923) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1923–1931).

Otto Höfler was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Vienna (~1921–1926) and Lund University (~1928–1934), later holding posts at the University of Kiel, Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich, and the University of Vienna.

Otto Neugebauer worked in history and archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Graz and Göttingen, he held posts at Göttingen, Copenhagen, Brown University, and the Institute for Advanced Study.

Otto Rosenberg worked in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at the Faculty of Oriental Studies of St. Petersburg University under Theodore Stcherbatsky and Sergey Oldenburg (~1906–1911), later serving as a professor at Saint Petersburg State University (~1917–1919).
Otto Stein was an Indology scholar who studied at the philosophy faculty of the German University of Prague from circa 1913 to 1921 under Moriz Winternitz.
Otto Strauss worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Paul Deussen from circa 1904 to 1911 and served as a professor at the University of Kiel from circa 1920 to 1935.

Otto von Böhtlingk worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University, under Franz Bopp (~1835–1839), and under Christian Lassen (~1839–1841). He was a member of the Russian Academy of Sciences (1842) and held a post at Jena (~1868–1885).

P. D. Premasiri is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Sri Jayawardenepura Maha Vidyalaya, the University of Ceylon, the University of Canterbury, and the University of Hawaii under Eliot Deutsch, later serving as professor at the University of Ceylon.

P. K. Mukhopadhyay works in philosophy and Indology. He was a Professor of Philosophy at Jadavpur University and served as a National Fellow at the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (attested 2009).

P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under traditional teachers Nilakantha and Vaidyanatha, graduated from the University of Madras (~1910–1914), and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Annamalai University from circa 1932 to 1947.

Padmanabh S. Jaini was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He held a professorship at the University of California, Berkeley, where he was attested as professor between 1977 and 2002, and as professor emeritus in 2016.

Palmira Brummett is a historian and archaeologist. She studied at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1968–1974) and the University of Chicago (~1984–1988), and she held a post at the University of Tennessee from circa 1989 to 2011.
Palmo Kyi is a scholar in the field of Tibetology. She studied under Hanna Havnevik, Rinzin Thargyal, and Per Kvaerne.

Pamela D. Winfield specializes in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She held a post at Temple University (attested 2001) and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Elon University (attested 2015–2017).

Pandurang Vaman Kane was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Mumbai (~1898–1908). He held posts at Elphinstone High School, Elphinstone College, Wilson College, the University of Mumbai, and was National Professor of Indology (~1959–1972).
Parashuram Krishna Gode was a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He served as Curator at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute from 1916 (or ~1919) to 1946 (or ~1961).

Parimal G. Patil specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard University (~1989–1993) and the University of Chicago (~1993–2002), and took up a post at Harvard University circa 2003.

Parul Dave-Mukherji works in Indology, philosophy, and history/archaeology. She completed her DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (1988–1991) and served as professor of Visual Studies and Art History at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2020).
